name: Weekly Pool Cleaning
title: Weekly Pool Cleaning & Maintenance Dallas–DFW | PoolBurg
description: Detailed weekly pool cleaning in Dallas–Fort Worth: visit tasks, water testing, brushing, vacuuming, filter and salt-system care, service notes, and pricing questions.
alt: PoolBurg weekly pool cleaning in a North Texas backyard
imagealt: Pool care image from PoolBurg’s weekly service page
lead: Weekly pool care is a repeating process of cleaning, testing, checking circulation, and recording what changed. The goal is a plan that fits your pool’s condition and use, with a clear boundary between normal maintenance, deep cleaning, and repair work.
promise: A steady routine. Fewer unanswered questions.
overview: The useful starting point is your pool’s condition today: its water clarity, debris load, equipment, and how often it is used. A maintained pool and a neglected green pool need different scopes. Confirm what the weekly plan includes before comparing monthly prices.
questions: What should happen during a weekly visit?

PoolBurg’s published weekly scope covers water testing and balancing, cleaning the floor and surfaces, basket care, equipment observations, filter and salt-system attention, and service notes. The actual work on a particular visit depends on the pool and agreed plan. Ask how deep cleaning, specialty treatments, and parts are distinguished from recurring work. The PoolBurg service checklist gives a useful comparison.
Why do brushing and vacuuming both matter?

They address different places where material collects. Brushing reaches walls, steps, benches, and other surfaces, while floor cleaning removes settled debris. A cleaner moving across the floor does not establish that every surface has been brushed. Explain which features your pool has, including a spa or shallow ledge, when confirming the cleaning plan.
Which water readings should be recorded?

Discuss sanitizer, pH, alkalinity, stabilizer, and calcium hardness as appropriate to the pool and current conditions. The visit record should identify what was measured, any adjustment made, and what needs attention afterward. Clear water is only one observation. The CDC’s home-pool testing guidance explains why sanitizer and pH checks also matter between service visits.
Do I need to test water between visits?

A weekly appointment does not mean the water remains unchanged until the next one. Swimming, weather, debris, and equipment operation can affect the pool between visits. Ask the team for an owner routine that follows your equipment and product instructions, including how to report abnormal readings. The CDC recommends regular testing more frequently than a weekly visit, particularly when use increases.
What if my pool uses a salt system?

Salt equipment produces chlorine; it does not replace physical cleaning, water testing, or filtration. Confirm how the plan handles the cell and operating readings, then use the saltwater maintenance guide for warning lights, scale, and questions about cleaning or diagnosis.
When is filter deep cleaning separate?

Filter condition and model determine the work. A routine check or model-appropriate attention during a visit can differ from disassembly, deep cleaning, inspection, and replacement elements. The filter-cleaning guide explains what to confirm when pressure, flow, or repeated cloudiness suggests a dedicated appointment.
Why does the pool look worse after a storm?

A storm can change debris load, water condition, and equipment operation. Tell the team about runoff, overflow, power interruptions, and visible changes instead of waiting for the usual visit without reporting the issue. If the pool has become green or heavily clouded, recovery work may need a different scope from ongoing care.
Can I start weekly care with a dirty pool?

Yes, request an assessment, but clarify the starting work. A pool with accumulated debris, green water, or a circulation fault may need a cleanup or repair before its normal routine is established. Compare one-time cleaning with recurring care so the first visit and ongoing price describe different tasks clearly.
How much does weekly pool cleaning cost?

Pool size, features, condition, debris, access, equipment, and the agreed service cadence influence the quote. Ask about standard chemical inclusions, specialty treatments, deep cleaning, and repair charges. Compare written scopes rather than the headline price alone. PoolBurg’s maintenance-routine guide connects the ongoing tasks to the pool’s needs.
What should my visit notes tell me?

A useful record explains the work completed, water readings and adjustments, equipment observations, anything that prevented normal service, and recommended next steps. Ask which findings require your approval, how to contact the team between visits, and what instructions apply after a treatment or change. The notes should help you understand the visit without claiming that one reading guarantees the entire week.

name: Pool Equipment Repair
title: Pool Equipment Repair in Dallas–DFW | PoolBurg
description: Pool pump, filter, heater, and control problems in Dallas–Fort Worth. Get clear answers about symptoms, repair versus replacement, and PoolBurg service.
alt: Pool pump equipment photographed by PoolBurg
imagealt: Technician servicing pool equipment on PoolBurg’s repair page
lead: A pump that will not start, a filter that will not clear the water, or controls that stop responding can all interrupt the same pool. PoolBurg’s Dallas–Fort Worth equipment repair service starts with the symptom and the system around it.
promise: Find the fault. Understand the options.
overview: Equipment works as a connected system. Pump speed, filter condition, valves, water level, and control settings can affect one another. Describe what changed and when it happens so the service request starts with useful evidence instead of an assumed failed part.
questions: Why won’t my pool pump start?

Possible causes include the power supply, controls, a motor problem, or a drive fault. A schedule or automation setting can also make a working pump appear unresponsive. Note the exact model, any displayed message, and whether the problem began after a power outage or another equipment change. Repeated breaker trips need qualified diagnosis rather than repeated resets.
Why is my pump running without flow?

A running motor does not prove that water is circulating properly. Low pool water, a suction-side air leak, restricted baskets, valve position, or an internal obstruction can affect prime and flow. If the pump is running dry, turn it off and request service. Photograph the equipment configuration rather than opening the motor or reaching into a running pump.
Does a leaking pump need replacing?

Not always. Water can escape at a lid seal, union, drain plug, shaft seal, or cracked housing. The repair decision depends on the actual leak point, motor condition, parts availability, and system compatibility. PoolBurg’s guide to leaking pump housings explains why a puddle beside the pump is not a complete diagnosis.
Why does my filter pressure keep rising?

A filter can load with debris during normal cleaning, but rapid repeat pressure changes can signal an ongoing water problem, cleaning issue, or restriction. Compare readings under similar operating conditions and report the clean baseline if you have it. Do not open a pressurized filter. A leaking tank or clamp needs service before normal operation resumes.
Should I repair or replace the equipment?

Compare the repair scope with the condition and compatibility of the whole system. A localized repair can make sense when the remaining equipment is sound. Replacement may be more practical when several components are failing or parts are unavailable. PoolBurg’s pump-and-filter replacement guide shows why a quote should identify equipment, installation, controls, and startup separately.
How much does pool equipment repair cost?

The failed component, diagnostic work, access, replacement parts, and any plumbing or control changes affect the quote. Ask what the assessment includes, whether the repair is separate, and what post-repair checks are planned. Share warranty documents if you have them; coverage must be confirmed for the specific equipment and fault.

name: Pool Leak Detection & Repair
title: Pool Leak Detection & Repair Dallas–DFW | PoolBurg
description: Pool losing water in Dallas–Fort Worth? Explore leak warning signs, evaporation versus leaks, inspection methods, and PoolBurg pool leak repair.
alt: PoolBurg technician using listening equipment to investigate a pool leak
imagealt: PoolBurg technician performing an underwater pool leak inspection
lead: You refill the pool, then the level drops again. Before assuming it is the Texas heat, look at the pattern. PoolBurg’s pool leak detection and repair service helps Dallas–Fort Worth owners investigate unexplained water loss and discuss a repair based on what is found.
promise: Trace the water loss. Then plan the repair.
overview: A skimmer leak, equipment-pad drip, underground line problem, and surface defect need different investigations. Useful details include how quickly the level changes, whether an autofill is running, and whether you notice wet soil or water around equipment. Those clues guide testing; they do not identify a leak on their own.
questions: Is my pool leaking or evaporating?

Evaporation varies with weather, wind, water temperature, and use, so a single universal daily allowance is not enough to diagnose a leak. Unexplained repeated refills deserve a closer look, especially when the pattern changes. A controlled comparison test can help distinguish water loss from evaporation, but an autofill, rain, splash-out, and different operating conditions can make the result misleading.
Why does the water stop at the skimmer?

A recurring stopping level can help narrow an investigation, but it does not prove a particular fitting is leaking. The skimmer body, its connection to the pool, nearby fittings, or another defect at that elevation may need inspection. PoolBurg’s guide to skimmer problems explains the clues worth documenting before repairs are chosen.
Can a pool leak underground?

Yes. Buried circulation plumbing can lose water without producing an obvious puddle beside the pool. Testing may include isolating appropriate lines, pressure testing, and locating a suspected fault. The approach depends on the plumbing layout and access. Wet ground is a useful observation, but irrigation and drainage can create similar signs.
How does pool leak detection work?

The investigation can combine a visual assessment with dye testing, listening equipment, underwater inspection, or plumbing tests where appropriate. Different methods answer different questions. Ask which parts of the pool and plumbing are included, what findings will be documented, and whether a follow-up location or repair visit may be required.
Does leak detection include the repair?

Confirm the scope before booking. Finding a leak and repairing it can involve different labor, materials, or access work. A localized fitting repair is different from reaching buried plumbing. Request an explanation of the identified fault, proposed repair, and any impact on tile, deck, landscaping, or equipment before approving the work.
How much does pool leak detection cost?

Pool and spa configuration, plumbing complexity, test coverage, access, and additional locating work affect pricing. Ask for the detection scope and any limits in writing. Do not compare a basic inspection with a quote that includes plumbing tests and repair; they may represent different work.

name: Pool Heating & Cooling
title: Pool Heating & Cooling in Dallas–DFW | PoolBurg
description: Pool heater not heating or pool water too warm? Explore Dallas–Fort Worth pool heating, heat pumps, chillers, repair questions, and PoolBurg service.
alt: Pool heater equipment photographed by PoolBurg
imagealt: Pool heating equipment shown on PoolBurg’s heating and cooling service page
lead: Too cold for the swim you planned. Too warm to feel refreshing. PoolBurg helps Dallas–Fort Worth pool owners discuss heater repairs, heat pumps, and cooling options around the equipment they have and the way they want to use the pool.
promise: A comfortable swim starts with the right plan.
overview: A gas heater, electric resistance heater, heat pump, and dedicated cooler do not behave the same way. The right discussion starts with the model, pool size, target temperature, season, available utilities, and whether the problem is a new failure or a long-standing performance limit.
questions: Why isn’t my pool heater heating?

The cause can involve operating mode, temperature settings, water flow, an error condition, or a component fault. Record the model and exact display message before a service visit. Different heater types require different tests. PoolBurg’s electric heater repair guide explains why identifying the equipment comes before buying a replacement part.
Why does my heater keep shutting off?

A heater may stop because it has reached the setpoint, is following a control schedule, or has detected an operating condition that interrupts heating. Restricted flow and sensor or control problems are possibilities, but a code alone does not prove a specific part failed. Share when the shutdown happens and whether water flow or other equipment changed at the same time.
Why is my heat pump so slow?

Heat pumps move heat from outdoor air into the pool, so performance depends on ambient conditions, water flow, runtime, and heat loss. A large temperature increase can take longer than owners expect, particularly in cool or windy conditions. PoolBurg’s heat-pump troubleshooting article separates operating expectations from symptoms that warrant a repair visit.
Can I cool my pool in summer?

Cooling options include compatible reversible heat pumps and dedicated pool-cooling equipment. A heater does not automatically provide cooling; the specific model must support it. Ask about the pool’s heat gain, desired result, equipment compatibility, and expected operating conditions before comparing units. North Texas weather and the pool’s exposure affect the outcome.
Should I choose a heater or heat pump?

Compare the way you use the pool with the available equipment and utilities. Heating a spa for occasional use is a different goal from maintaining pool temperature over a season. Discuss heat-up expectations, outdoor conditions, energy use, space, sound, and installation requirements. A quote should identify the equipment and the supporting plumbing, electrical, gas, or control work.
What affects heating and cooling costs?

Pool volume, target temperature, outdoor conditions, runtime, heat loss, and equipment efficiency all affect operation. Installation costs also depend on utilities, pad layout, controls, and plumbing. Ask for a site-specific scope rather than a guaranteed bill or temperature result. For a repair, confirm the diagnostic charge and recommended work separately.

name: Pool Acid Washing & Stain Care
title: Pool Acid Washing & Stain Care Dallas–DFW | PoolBurg
description: Stained pool plaster in Dallas–Fort Worth? Explore acid washing, recurring rust stains, surface condition, cleaning versus resurfacing, and PoolBurg service.
alt: Pool acid washing service image from PoolBurg
imagealt: Pool acid washing comparison image supplied in PoolBurg’s media library
lead: Stains will not brush away. The finish looks patchy. You want a cleaner pool without choosing the wrong treatment. PoolBurg’s acid washing and surface-care service starts by looking at the stain and the condition of the finish.
promise: Understand the stain before treating the surface.
overview: Acid washing is a surface treatment, not a repair for every discolored pool. The finish type, remaining condition, previous treatments, and source of staining all matter. A worn or failing finish may need renovation instead of another aggressive cleaning.
questions: Will an acid wash remove pool stains?

It can improve some staining on suitable pool finishes, but the result depends on the stain and the surface. Organic marks, metal staining, scale, and damage beneath a finish do not all respond to the same approach. Ask for an assessment of the stain type, treatment options, and likely limitations before agreeing to drain or chemically treat the pool.
Why do rust stains keep coming back?

Rust-colored marks can relate to fill water, metal debris, fixtures, or an underlying source beneath the finish. Cleaning the visible stain alone may leave that source in place. PoolBurg’s guide to recurring pool rust stains explains why the pattern and location matter when deciding whether cleaning or further repair is appropriate.
Do I need acid washing or resurfacing?

The distinction is the condition of the finish. A sound but stained surface may be a cleaning candidate. Areas that are failing, worn through, or separating require a different assessment. Surface cleaning does not rebuild missing material or repair structural movement. If the finish is deteriorating, compare a pool renovation scope before paying for a cosmetic treatment.
Does a green pool need acid washing?

Not automatically. Green water can involve sanitation, circulation, debris, or metals; a green color does not by itself establish that the finish needs acid washing. Start with water and equipment assessment. PoolBurg’s explanation of green water after rain shows why the cause should be identified before choosing the treatment.
Will the pool need to be drained?

Some surface work involves draining, but that decision depends on the treatment, pool construction, weather, groundwater, and site conditions. Have the team determine the method and timing. Do not empty the pool in preparation for a quote. Ask who handles draining, discharge arrangements, refilling, and water balancing if those steps are part of the work.
How much does a pool acid wash cost?

Pool size, staining, finish condition, access, preparation, and the agreed drain-and-refill work affect the quote. Confirm what happens if the assessment shows that the finish is too worn for the proposed treatment. Ask whether water, refill time, startup care, or repair work are separate responsibilities.

name: Pool Remodeling
title: Pool Remodeling in Dallas–DFW | PoolBurg
description: Plan a pool remodel in Dallas–Fort Worth with PoolBurg. Get answers about resurfacing, tile, coping, equipment, project order, timelines, and quote scope.
alt: Pool remodeling project image supplied by PoolBurg
imagealt: Pool project photograph from PoolBurg’s remodeling service gallery
lead: Rough plaster, tired tile, loose edges, or equipment that no longer fits the way you swim: a pool remodel should solve the problems behind the worn appearance. PoolBurg helps Dallas–Fort Worth owners turn those concerns into a coordinated renovation scope.
promise: Fix what matters. Then choose the finish.
overview: A pool refresh can range from targeted surface work to changes involving equipment, tile, coping, decking, and surrounding details. Start by separating necessary repairs from the upgrades you want. That makes it easier to compare proposals and avoid reopening new work for an overlooked problem.
questions: Does my pool need a full remodel?

Not every worn pool needs every component replaced. A localized stain, isolated repair, or equipment fault can call for a smaller scope. Widespread finish failure, recurring leaks, damaged edges, and several aging systems may justify a coordinated project. Ask for a condition assessment that identifies what can stay as well as what should change.
Is resurfacing the same as remodeling?

Resurfacing focuses on the pool’s interior finish. Remodeling can also include tile, coping, equipment, lighting, plumbing, deck details, and layout-related upgrades. Define those boundaries in the quote. If you mainly want a cleaner appearance, compare stain and surface care with finish replacement before choosing a bigger project.
Should leaks be fixed before remodeling?

Active water loss and underlying defects should be investigated before new finishes conceal the area. Planning plumbing and equipment access early can prevent cutting into recently completed work. PoolBurg’s pool-and-backyard remodel guide explains why hidden repairs and utilities belong near the beginning of the plan.
Can I replace tile and coping together?

They can be coordinated within one project, but the existing condition and connections matter. Discuss the bond beam, waterline, coping, adjoining deck, movement joints, and drainage so material choices fit the construction. A proposal should explain preparation and any underlying repairs rather than describing the work only by tile color or coping style.
How long does a pool remodel take?

Timing depends on demolition, repairs, materials, access, weather, inspections where applicable, and the finish system’s startup requirements. Ask for a staged schedule with the conditions that can change it. A finished-looking surface does not necessarily mean the pool is ready for normal use; confirm filling, brushing, chemistry, heating, and swimming instructions for the selected finish.
How much does pool remodeling cost?

The largest difference between quotes is often what they include. Surface-only work is different from a project that also addresses tile, coping, equipment, plumbing, or decking. PoolBurg’s restoration-cost guide helps separate those categories. Request an itemized scope, allowances, exclusions, and a process for approving work discovered after demolition.
